data.name: Fortnite
data.sellPolicyNote: Online game with anti-cheat; client mods can get players banned, so sales need review.

engineNotes.title: Safety
lines: Anti-cheat: Easy Anti-Cheat. Melty installs no loader for this game and never mods its client, so in a mashup it is only a companion: its content is read from the player's own installed copy while they play the other (moddable) game, and it is never launched with a mod — so there is no anti-cheat exposure and no account risk. Build the mashup in the moddable game.

engineNotes.title: What a mashup can't use
lines: Agents building on it found its game content (IoStore containers, .utoc/.ucas) encrypted (Oct 2026): plan nothing that reads or replaces it, and don't promise it to the creator.

engineNotes.title: Players in a session
lines: From a UE4SS Lua mod, FindFirstOf("GameStateBase") gives the game state, and its PlayerArray lists a PlayerState per player: GetPlayerName(), PlayerId and UniqueId.
PlayerId is the same number on every client in the session. UniqueId's text carries the platform id (a 17-digit SteamID64) on some builds only, so fall back to PlayerId.
GameStateBase:GetServerWorldTimeSeconds() is the server's clock, the same on every client: use it to line players up in time.
This reader was written with no record of a run on a shipped game: confirm each read in the game.

engineNotes.title: Camera
lines: UEHelpers.GetPlayerController() (or FindFirstOf("PlayerController")), then its PlayerCameraManager: GetCameraLocation(), GetCameraRotation() and GetFOVAngle(). Lua gets no view matrix.
Left-handed with Z up, in centimetres: X is forward, Y is right. The field of view is horizontal unless the game changes its aspect-ratio constraint.

Without UE4SS, a native plugin can walk GWorld, OwningGameInstance, LocalPlayers[0], PlayerController, PlayerCameraManager, then the cached camera view. Positions are doubles on UE5 and floats on UE4.

engineNotes.title: Key bindings and input
lines: UE5 games (Enhanced Input) keep bindings in assets, not a file: read playerController.PlayerInput.EnhancedActionMappings, and poll GetActionValue(action) each frame for what is pressed.

Older games: StaticFindObject("/Script/Engine.InputSettings"):GetCDO() has ActionMappings and AxisMappings, and the file is {localappdata}/<Project>/Saved/Config/Windows/Input.ini (or WindowsNoEditor, WinGDK), lines like +ActionMappings=(ActionName="Jump",...,Key=SpaceBar).
Reading bindings this way was never run on a shipped game.

engineNotes.title: Worth knowing
lines: Read the engine on the game thread (LoopInGameThreadAfterFrames, LoopInGameThreadWithDelay, or ExecuteInGameThread) and wrap each read in pcall: an error inside a LoopAsync callback silently ends the loop.
FindFirstOf("PlayerController") finds nothing on the main menu, and never returns class defaults.
RegisterHook can't hook delegate functions or C++ virtuals, so poll instead of hooking input handlers or the viewport's render.

UE4SS 3 mods go in ue4ss/Mods/<Name>/Scripts/main.lua with an enabled.txt in <Name>. UE 5.4 and later can need a newer experimental UE4SS than the one Melty installs, so prove the mod loads in the real game first.
UE4SS runs plain Lua 5.4: no FFI and no high-resolution clock.
